summary: Customer is developing a hot polymer extrusion process that contains an active pharmaceutical ingredient and asks whether an optical measurement can detect composition changes in the melt. The process interface is hot and may suffer material build-up. They have offline assays and want an initial comparison plan plus the questions to settle before choosing a probe.

facts_stated.text: Process is a hot polymer extrusion process
The formulation incorporates an active pharmaceutical ingredient
The measurement would be made on the melt during processing
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: while the melt is being processed

facts_stated.text: The process interface may be exposed to material build-up
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: may be exposed to material build up

targets.variable: composition changes in the melt (species, range and magnitude not stated)
targets.enquiry_quote: detect composition changes while the melt is being processed

physical_state.enquiry_quote: while the melt is being processed

process.value: stated only as hot, no value given
possible material build-up on the interface
process.enquiry_quote: may be exposed to material build up

customer_premises.claim: Composition changes in the melt can be detected optically in-process; this is the question to investigate, but whether the change is optically detectable at all is unverified.
customer_premises.enquiry_quote: detect composition changes while the melt is being processed

customer_premises.claim: Offline assays can serve as a reference for an in-line measurement.
The hot interface and possible material build-up are the governing constraints on method choice.
customer_premises.enquiry_quote: the process interface is hot and may be exposed to material build up

unknowns: Which active pharmaceutical ingredient is the target and its concentration range
Magnitude and rate of the composition change that must be detected
Polymer matrix and other formulation components, and whether they interfere optically
Physical state and optical behaviour of the melt at the measurement point (clear, turbid, scattering, absorbing)
Temperature value at the process interface
Installation point on the extruder and distance/path length to the interface
Rate and nature of material build-up, and cleaning requirements
Required accuracy, detection limit and response time
Details of the offline assays (reference method, sampling, comparability)
Whether the API or a justified fluorescent indicator is present
